event.subtitle: A group exhibition of 18 artists presented by MCLIV
event.statement: Artists from all walks of life come together in one cohesive exhibition. Every work shares the same 16 × 20-inch format; each artist brings a distinct point of view.
event.venuePublicName: The Port Authority Midtown Bus Terminal

artists.name: Madsteez
artists.artistBio:
Mark Paul Deren (MADSTEEZ) was born on June 23, 1980. Born blind in his left eye and with three first names, Mark Paul Deren, aka MADSTEEZ, has built a visual language that refuses to sit still.

Based in Brooklyn, New York, MADSTEEZ works across painting, murals, installation, and large-scale public art, creating a world where portraiture collides with abstraction and recognizable figures dissolve into explosive fields of color, movement, and controlled chaos. His unmistakable palette—electric, saturated, and unapologetically loud—has transformed everything from intimate canvases to entire buildings and public spaces around the world.

At the core of MADSTEEZ’s work is a constant push and pull between precision and spontaneity. Faces, figures, and familiar forms emerge from layers of expressive marks, warped proportions, and kinetic fields of pigment, creating imagery that feels simultaneously deliberate and unrestrained.

Over a career spanning more than two decades, MADSTEEZ has painted murals across five continents and collaborated with brands and cultural institutions including Nike, the NBA, Audi, Warner Brothers, Amazon and the New York Knicks to nane a few. His subjects have ranged from cultural icons to deeply personal characters, all filtered through the same singular universe.

Whether working at the scale of a canvas, a basketball court, or the side of a building, MADSTEEZ approaches each surface as an opportunity to disrupt the familiar—turning it into something louder, stranger, more colorful, and WEENified.

artists.name: Trouble Andrew
artists.artistBio:
Trouble Andrew, also known as Trevor Andrew and GucciGhost, is a multidisciplinary artist from Nova Scotia, Canada. His practice spans painting, drawing, sculpture, music, digital art, and fashion.

Through his GucciGhost imagery, Andrew transforms found objects and clothing while questioning ideas of authenticity, luxury, and value. His reinterpretation of Gucci's visual language led to a collaboration with the fashion house for its Fall/Winter 2016 collection.

artists.name: Hoxxoh
artists.artistBio:
Douglas "HoxxoH" Hoekzema—part machine, part mad-scientist. Weaving his paints in and out like a human-loom, he uses logarithmic spirals to chronicle the passage of time and the universal parallels between control and chaos. Implementing sacred geometry, Hoekzema is able to use the earth’s gravitational pull to layer minute upon minute, channeling the cosmos and the individual mechanisms that hold life together.

Also known for his murals and spray work, Hoekzema references the spiritual, natural, and instinctual pull toward balance; meeting two polar opposites in the middle to discover their inevitable likeness. With restraint being an ever-present key to his practice, Hoekzema actively participates as a module in the grander system, consciously pushing his patterns and designs to the point of synergetic equilibrium.

artists.name: Jerami Dean Goodwin
artists.artistBio:
Jerami Dean Goodwin (b. 1989) is a multidisciplinary artist based in New York City whose practice moves between painting, mixed media, collage, photography, and installation. His work is rooted in an ongoing exploration of culture, memory, and the visual language of contemporary life. Drawing from the imagery and ephemera that surround him, Goodwin treats artmaking as a process of collecting, filtering, and reinterpreting information—approaching the studio almost like an antenna, absorbing fragments of popular culture, history, advertising, and everyday experience before transforming them into new visual compositions.

Goodwin’s practice is informed by both street and fine art, reflecting his background as a muralist and self-taught tattoo artist before developing a broader studio practice. His experimental process incorporates unconventional techniques, including fire extinguisher-applied paint, silkscreen, collage, and layered mixed media, creating works that balance spontaneity with intention. He has exhibited his work in galleries and exhibitions across the United States and previously operated 99 Bowery, an independent gallery in New York City dedicated to showcasing emerging and established artists. Goodwin continues to live and work in New York, where he explores the intersection of art, culture, and contemporary visual language.

artists.name: Cavier Coleman
artists.materialMedia: Acrylic latex, oil pastel, paper collage on canvas
artists.artistBio: Cavier Coleman (b. 1988, Saginaw, Michigan) stands as a beacon in the contemporary art world. His work embodies an avant-garde spirit, driven by an insatiable curiosity and a relentless quest for truth. It also serves as a stimulant in the dialogue between the personal and the societal. The attitudes expressed through the work’s titles and thematic engagements reflect his acute awareness of his role not only as a creator, but also as a visionary and thinker. Cavier’s paintings are in dialogue with works by the masters, much like the output he is responsible for in his other creative careers in music and photography. He echoes the genius of historical figures to build context around his favored discourses: truth, civic character, and the elements of society that we all share and revel in. The result is art that is fun, challenging, and overwhelmingly honest.

artists.name: Gianni Lee
artists.materialMedia: Oil on canvas, hand-beaded elements and door curtain
artists.artistBio: Gianni Lee is a multidisciplinary artist whose practice explores Black identity, futurism, mythology, technology, and the visual language of contemporary culture. Working across painting, sculpture, fashion, music, and installation, Lee creates worlds where historical memory and imagined futures collide. Born in Philadelphia, Lee’s visual language draws from the cultural landscapes that shaped him—comic books, anime, manga, video games, street culture, fashion, and Afrofuturism—while incorporating references to African spirituality, ritual, and diasporic identity. His work frequently reimagines the Black figure within speculative environments, using saturated color, graphic symbolism, sculptural forms, and unconventional materials to question how Black bodies and histories are represented, preserved, and mythologized. Lee’s recent paintings move increasingly between portraiture and object-making. Works such as KARA-TONE (2026) extend the painted image into the physical space through hand-beaded elements, textile, and sculptural framing. The resulting works operate somewhere between portrait, artifact, shrine, and contemporary relic—objects that feel as though they could belong simultaneously to an imagined future and an excavated past. Alongside his studio practice, Lee has developed projects spanning fashion, cultural programming, music, and creative direction through Gianni Lee Studio, reflecting an approach to art that exists beyond a single medium or discipline. His practice is ultimately concerned with world-building: creating visual languages and objects that allow Black identity to exist outside of familiar historical narratives and into new, speculative futures.

artists.name: Steph Costello
artists.artistBio: Steph Costello (b. 1979) is a Brooklyn-based artist who uses painting and drawing to create imaginative urban constructions. She has shown her work with The Bronx Museum, Pierogi Gallery in New York, and La Pan Gallery in Barcelona. She is a recipient of mural grants from The NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, the NYC Department of Transportation, New York Health and Hospitals, and The Brooklyn Arts Council.

artists.name: John Black
artists.artistBio: Born in southern West Virginia, John Black is an American visual artist whose practice explores ritual, repetition, communication and symbolic language through abstract painting and sculpture. Working primarily with acrylic paint and a distinctive roller technique, he has developed an evolving visual vocabulary he describes as Structural Symbolism, where repeated gestures become meditative acts that investigate ancestry, color, memory and cultural exchange. Research into ancient cultures, textiles, archaeology and systems of visual communication informs an intuitive studio practice rooted equally in discipline and discovery.

artists.name: Smurfo
artists.artistBio: Christopher Weeden (b. 1989) known as Smurfo UDirty is a Brooklyn born multifaceted artist based in New York City. His artistic journey began with street art, graffiti and storytelling. In fact, it’s not uncommon to walk the streets of Bushwick and trace the Smurfo tags throughout the neighborhood. “Brooklyn is urban history that needs to be preserved” and as part of that preservation Weeden acts as a documentarian; His goals are to preserve history, tell stories that matter to the urban landscape of New York and to promote free thought while addressing all of the issues that society cavalierly sweeps under the rug.

artists.name: Jason Rohlf
artists.artistBio:
Jason Rohlf born in Milwaukee, WI 1970. Attended the University of Milwaukee for three years on a Layton Scholarship but did not finish his degree. Currently a Brooklyn-based artist working primarily in painting. His works range from his extensive Shop Rag Project to massive painted tarps up to 12 feet tall. His practice is heavily process-driven and reveals a deep understanding and investigation of materials and color. He has resided in Williamsburg with his family since 1999.

Each piece is the field for continued exploration as countless layers of collage, mediums and acrylic paint coalesce to become a finished painting. Conveying an urban palimpsest, elements of relief, affect, transformation, and time all become present in the work.

Rohlf’s work has been reviewed in The New York Times, Hyperallergic, Time Out Chicago, and Milwaukee Magazine among others. Notable solo and group exhibitions have taken place at Gold Scopophila (Montclair, NJ), Tory Folliard Gallery (Milwaukee, WI), ReInstitute (Millerton, NY), Rick Wester (New York, NY), Pentimenti Gallery (Philadelphia, PA), and Pelham Art Center (Pelham, NY), among others. He attended the Sam & Adel Golden Paint Foundation at Golden Artist Colors, New Berlin, NY. He has produced public arts projects for the MTA (Arts for Transit) at Far Rockaway in Queens and the New York Public Schools at PSQ 174 in Rego Park, Queens.

artists.name: King Saladeen
artists.artworkName: Faces Of Success: No Middle Cla$$
artists.materialMedia: Oil pastel, mixed media on canvas
artists.artistBio: King Saladeen is a contemporary American artist whose work bridges fine art, street culture, and sports through a distinct visual language rooted in symbolism, repetition, and emotion. Working primarily in painting and collectible formats, Saladeen transforms familiar icons, athletes, mascots, numbers, and cultural references into layered works that explore ambition, identity, and legacy. His artistic style is defined by bold mark-making, textured surfaces, and recurring motifs that create a sense of movement and narrative. Each piece reflects an intuitive creative process, where structure and spontaneity coexist. Saladeen often builds his works through layering, allowing imperfections and raw gestures to remain visible, reinforcing the authenticity behind each piece. Inspired by personal experience, cultural history, and the emotional connection people have to sports and competition, Saladeen’s work speaks to moments of pressure, triumph, and perseverance. His approach turns art into an extension of lived experience meant not only to be viewed, but felt. Saladeen’s work is unique in its ability to function both as fine art and as collectible objects, making it accessible to a broad audience while maintaining artistic integrity. His collaborations and commissions span sports, fashion, and cultural institutions, and his work has been showcased in galleries, pop-up exhibitions, and high-profile brand partnerships. Collectors are drawn to Saladeen’s work for its emotional resonance, limited availability, and cultural relevance. Each piece represents a moment in time capturing the energy of competition, creativity, and personal expression making his work both visually striking and meaningfully collectible. April, 1983

artists.name: AKLO
artists.materialMedia: Spray Paint & Paint Marker on Canvas with knife lacerations
artists.artistBio:
Born in Washington Heights, New York City, AKLO is a multidisciplinary artist and software developer. He was mentored in abstract expressionism by Flatbush native Pierre Bernard Francillion, a contemporary of Jean-Michel Basquiat. His work has been exhibited at the New Museum, Superchief Gallery, and Wallplay.

His music videos for Atlantic Records artists have earned more than 100 million views on YouTube. His work has been published in Vogue, PAPER, Dazed, i-D, Hypebeast, WorldStarHipHop, Complex, and more.

artists.name: Lola Jiblazee
artists.artistBio: Lola Jiblazee (b. 1985, Tbilisi, Georgia) is a New York–based multidisciplinary artist working in painting, textiles, and mixed media. Raised in Tbilisi during a period defined by political instability, pervasive poverty, gang violence, substance crises, and blackouts, Jiblazee developed a lasting interest in how people find structure in chaos and uncertainty. Having studied traditional iconography in their youth, Jiblazee was drawn to its deliberate flatness, restricted depth, and emotionless precision of form. Following their immigration to the United States in their early twenties, Jiblazee integrated these structural elements into their work, finding a balance between figure, symbol, and abstraction. Jiblazee looks at the space between inherited history, personal memory, and everyday reality.

artists.name: Gazoo ToTheMoon
artists.artistBio:
Legendary artist Gazoo To The Moon creates artworks that speak beyond the surface.

While he is widely known for his street art and iconic "To The Moon" tag, his creativity encompasses even more. His inspiring energy and visionary storytelling are reflected in his unique artwork. Due to his extensive knowledge of working with various materials, Gazoo’s visions are limitless; he also uses the carpentry skills he has gained working as a set designer and builder to craft three-dimensional wooden art pieces.

His deep connection to his craft and creativity has established him as a significant figure in urban culture, where he continues to inspire and influence the contemporary art scene.

Gazoo has roots in Montserrat, since his early years he is based in New York City.

artists.name: NotYourMuse
artists.materialMedia: Acrylic, spray paint and ink on premium cotton canvas
artists.artistBio: NotYourMuse is a New York–based artist, curator, and entrepreneur born in 1990. She is known for creating work that bridges fine art, fashion, technology, and immersive experiences. Since launching her career in 2013, Muse has developed a distinctive visual language rooted in personal narrative, nature, and a deeper spiritual connection—expressed through bold, playful, and thought-provoking compositions.

artists.name: Keya Tama
artists.artistBio: Keya Tama was born in 1997 in Cape Town, South Africa and moved to America in 2019. His work has been the focus of numerous exhibitions and mural projects including the Straat museum, Amsterdam; The Museum of Anthropology, Canary Islands; and Subliminal Projects, Los Angeles, among others. Tama currently lives and works in New York.

artists.name: Kevin Cincotta
artists.artistBio: Kevin Cincotta (b. 1997) is a New York City-based visual artist whose work explores the relationship between people, place, and the natural world through bold color, simplified forms, and symbolic imagery. Drawing from ecology, folklore, memory, and regional histories, his work combines elements of magical realism and visual storytelling to create scenes that feel both familiar and imagined. His practice spans canvas and public murals, creating a world that viewers can experience in both intimate and monumental settings.

artists.name: Esteban
artists.artistBio: Esteban Caasi is a New York native artist. A painter and a Tattoo Artist. He has 20 years experience in tattooing and currently as the owner of the small shop on Elizabeth Street.
